controls.title: Cybersecurity policy
controls.objective: A cybersecurity policy is approved by leadership, communicated to staff, and reviewed at least every 12 months.

evidence.description: Policy with approval and review dates

questions.text: Is there a cybersecurity policy approved by leadership and reviewed in the last 12 months?
questions.guidance: Partial: approved but last reviewed more than 12 months ago.

questions.text: Is the policy communicated to all staff, with acknowledgement recorded?

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Roles and accountability
controls.objective: A named executive is accountable for cybersecurity risk and roles are documented.

questions.text: Is a named executive accountable for cybersecurity risk, with documented cybersecurity roles and responsibilities?
questions.guidance: Partial: roles documented but no named accountable executive.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Risk management strategy
controls.objective: Risk appetite is documented and risks are recorded in a register using a standard scoring method.

evidence.description: Risk appetite statement and risk register

questions.text: Is there a documented risk appetite or tolerance statement approved by leadership?
Is there a risk register that scores cybersecurity risks with a defined method and was updated in the last 6 months?
questions.guidance: Partial: register exists but stale or without a scoring method.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Supplier security requirements
controls.objective: Suppliers are inventoried and ranked by criticality, and contracts with critical suppliers include security requirements.

evidence.description: Supplier list with criticality and sample contracts

questions.text: Is there a supplier inventory ranked by criticality?
Percentage of critical supplier contracts that include security requirements (breach notification, right to assess, data handling)

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Legal and regulatory requirements register
controls.objective: Cybersecurity and privacy legal, regulatory, and contractual obligations are recorded with owners.

questions.text: Is there a register of cybersecurity and privacy obligations (laws, regulations, contracts) with an owner for each?
questions.guidance: Partial: list exists without owners or not updated in 12 months.

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29

controls.title: Security program oversight
controls.objective: Leadership reviews security risk and program performance at least every 6 months and records decisions.

questions.text: Months since leadership last reviewed cybersecurity risk and program performance, per minutes
questions.guidance: Use the date of the last minutes that cover the review.

questions.text: Do the review minutes record decisions or adjustments to the security strategy?

references.source: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0
references.note: wording to be checked against CSWP 29
